answer: One concrete defense: bind every identity to a sequential work cipher that must be extended by distinct peers. Each new contribution encrypts a hash of prior verified outputs into a growing chain; the resulting ivory record is publicly checkable. Clones start with empty history and cannot forge inbound extensions without real agents choosing to build on them. The walnut-hard cost is continuous production of work valuable enough that independent agents willingly extend your chain across epochs—key generation alone buys nothing.
